content.text: Open elective is the succession law of holy orders , mercenaries , republics and most theocracies . It is also used as a fallback for titles of independent feudal rulers, that have neither an heir that qualifies under the succession law of the title, valid heirs under the fallback primogeniture or seniority successions, nor feudal vassals that could inherit instead.
Open elective gives the title, upon the death of the title holder, to an eligible courtier of said title holder. If there are no eligible courtiers, one gets generated.

Potential heirs for holy orders need to be adult male courtiers with the same religion as the title holder and a positive "succession score" (cf. next paragraph). Being the prospective heir to a feudal, tribal or theocratic title disqualifies that courtier from the holy order's succession.
Besides that, being imprisoned by a ruler other than the title holder also removes a candidate from the line of succession.
To determine the ranking of the eligible courtiers they get sorted by a 'succession score', with the highest scorer becoming the first in line to inherit.

Theocratic titles of religious heads (e.g. the Ecumenical Patriarch, the Coptic Pope (for Miaphysitism), or the Manichean Yamag) always go straight to generating a new character for the title upon succession, even when suitable courtiers are available.

That doesn't apply though to intermediate religious heads of autocephalous religions like the patriarchs of the Eastern Orthodoxy . Those just follow the succession described below like other theocracies with open elective succession.

Potential heirs for theocracies need to be adult male courtiers (even if the religion allows female bishops/priests) with the same religion as the title holder and a positive "succession score" (cf. next paragraph). Besides that, being imprisoned by a ruler other than the title holder also removes a candidate from the line of succession.

For the fallback succession of tribal and feudal titles male courtiers qualify as potential heirs even underage ones. Women and girls are valid succession candidates, if the title's succession is not exclusively agnatic. The potential heir needs to have the same religious group as the current title holder.
Some of the usual disqualifications for succession like being heir to a theocracy do apply, others like being a bastard do not apply.

Besides that, being imprisoned by a ruler other than the title holder also removes a candidate from the line of succession. A potential candidate also needs a positive "succession score" (cf. next paragraph) to be eligible.

items.text: Sending Gifts : Increasing the wealth of a candidate courtier through gifts, lets the player pretty much choose which courtier will inherit in case of the title holder's death, which in turn can be used to get a candidate in power that is more likely to accept a vassalization offer, or a child or a woman that can be attacked by weak claims, etc.

Sending high prestige courtiers : Marrying high prestige courtiers into a foreign court by using matrilineal marriage for men and regular marriage for women can also influence the open elective succession

Imprisoning courtiers : if the player is hostile to the current title holder, due to raiding or war, they might be able to capture courtiers through sieges or battles and thus also remove said courtiers from the succession
